correctness.rationale: The Fourier fourth norm is a positive integer linear combination of nonconstant phase characters after subtracting the exact mean. Cubic Haar expectation selects only zero-sum character triples and cannot cancel. Each four-term progression creates exactly 12 disjoint ordered products with coefficient 16 (2*2*4), yielding 192 per progression. The four-point distribution proof enumerates the only possible pair-sum collisions, then proves joint Haar independence of nonparallel three-term characters. An exact integer checker on the current standalone artifact verifies 1602 distinct four-, five-, and six-point supports including the variance and sharp case. These checks are corroborative and not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: For arbitrary sparse frequency supports the third centered moment is a relevant distributional asymmetry statistic for random-phase fourth energy. The new sharp bound identifies guaranteed arithmetic contributions beyond known variance counts, and the complete four-frequency classification distinguishes symmetric from asymmetric fourth-energy laws with a nonzero standardized skewness 1/sqrt(3). This is a motivated natural cutoff in sparse Fourier/aperture statistics; neither a routine numerical improvement nor a rephrasing of the prior variance result.
